question: On the credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate established by EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378, over a frozen multi-host pool SEPARATELY CONFIRMED DURING DESIGN to contain DEEP (hop>=3) state items on >=2 distinct hosts/engines (>=10 total, >=3 per host), what fraction of those DEEP items is reachable in <= K=3 fresh-agent GETs using ANY of the five frozen site-native discovery channels (ROBOTS_SITEMAP, SITEMAP_XML, ON_SITE_SEARCH, RSS_ATOM, JSON_LD) -- with a preregistered materiality threshold of 0.50 on >=2 hosts deciding whether shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier (persistence of paths is not the optimization target; effort moves to discovery and substrate expansion) versus fresh deep-instance acquisition remaining path-bound with a computable persistence break-even surface?
hypothesis: Site-native discovery channels provide O(1) reachability (<=K=3 GETs) for a material fraction (>=0.50) of DEEP state items on at least two distinct hosts, demonstrating that shortest-path hop is not a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier for discovery-enabled acquisition. If true, persistent path/procedure caching is not the primary optimization target; effort should shift to discovery-channel coverage and substrate expansion.

falsifier.description: Arithmetically checkable before freeze and satisfiable in both directions on the frozen pool.
falsifier.positive_branch: If the fraction of DEEP items reachable in <=K GETs via ANY site-native discovery channel is >= materiality_threshold on >= min_hosts_with_threshold distinct hosts, then shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier for discovery-enabled acquisition. Persistent path caching is not the optimization target; effort moves to discovery and substrate expansion.
falsifier.negative_branch: If that fraction is below materiality_threshold on fewer than min_hosts_with_threshold hosts, then even with site-native discovery, fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound. Persistence of paths/procedures retains a measurable, depth-dependent amortization surface whose break-even can be computed from real re-derivation cost.
falsifier.per_channel_disclosure: Must report per-channel coverage (fraction of DEEP items reachable via that channel alone) and explicitly list any channel that yields zero admitted DEEP items rather than counting it as a null.

operational_definitions.substrate: HTTP GET only via Python stdlib urllib; TLS verified; frozen User-Agent 'SPIDER-research-frontier-38013774272/1.0'; timeout 12s; max response body 600000 bytes; redirects followed; no credentials, cookies, browser, Docker, model key or write verb.
operational_definitions.navigation_graph: Directed graph whose nodes are defragmented same-host http(s) URLs (same registrable host as the seed's final URL) and whose edges are <a href> links parsed from fetched HTML in document order. Non-http(s) schemes and asset extensions (png,jpg,jpeg,gif,svg,ico,css,js,pdf,zip,gz,woff,woff2,ttf,otf,mp4,webp,xml,rss,atom,epub,mobi,mp3,ogg,djvu,exe,iso) are excluded. JS-generated links are NOT edges.
operational_definitions.hop_distance: Graph shortest-path length in edges from the seed root (hop 0) to a page's URL, measured by the frozen BFS policy (item-blind FIFO document-order, budget 250, depth cap 6). The seed URL itself is hop 0.
operational_definitions.state_carrying_item: A (page_url, control_name, control_type) tuple where the fetched page contains at least one named form control: an <input> with a non-empty name attribute or a <select> with a non-empty name attribute. The page is the observable; the item's hop is the page's hop.

bands.MID_excluded: hop == 2 (reported descriptively; excluded from the primary NEAR-vs-DEEP contrast)

operational_definitions.frozen_policy: Item-blind FIFO breadth-first crawl in document order from the seed root; per-site page budget B=250; depth cap D=6; each URL fetched at most once; the crawl stops as soon as the target page is fetched (for a per-item RED cost) or when budget/depth is exhausted (for the structural pass).

discovery_channels.ROBOTS_SITEMAP: Fetch robots.txt at host root; parse Sitemap: directives; fetch each referenced sitemap URL; parse XML (sitemap index or urlset) to extract URL entries. A channel succeeds for an item if the item's page URL appears in any parsed sitemap and the item page is fetched successfully (2xx) within K GETs total.
discovery_channels.SITEMAP_XML: Fetch /sitemap.xml and /sitemap_index.xml at host root; parse XML (sitemap index or urlset) to extract URL entries. Same success criterion as ROBOTS_SITEMAP.
discovery_channels.ON_SITE_SEARCH: Locate search form on host root or known search page; extract action URL and query parameter name; construct search query using the item's control_name as search term; fetch results page; parse result links (anchor hrefs). A channel succeeds if the item's page URL appears in result links and the item page is fetched successfully (2xx) within K GETs total.
discovery_channels.RSS_ATOM: Find <link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml|application/atom+xml"> in HTML head of host root; fetch feed; parse entries for link/guid URLs. A channel succeeds if the item's page URL appears in feed entries and the item page is fetched successfully (2xx) within K GETs total.
discovery_channels.JSON_LD: Fetch item page HTML; parse <script type="application/ld+json"> elements; extract URL properties from structured data (e.g., @id, url, mainEntityOfPage). A channel succeeds if the item's page URL is extracted and the item page is fetched successfully (2xx) within K GETs total (note: this channel requires fetching the item page first, so it uses 2 GETs: item page + JSON-LD parse; the spare GET covers redirects).

operational_definitions.k_budget: K=3 GETs per item per channel: 1 discovery GET (sitemap, search, feed, or JSON-LD fetch) + 1 item-page GET + 1 spare for redirect/validation. For JSON_LD the discovery GET IS the item-page GET. A channel succeeds for an item if the item URL is discovered and the item page fetched successfully (2xx) within K GETs.
operational_definitions.hop_confirmation: Shortest-path hop for each admitted DEEP item is confirmed via the SAME link-following BFS used in EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378 (static <a href> parsing, same-host, depth<=6, budget 250). Hop and discovery reachability are distinct observables measured on the same item set.

baselines.role: comparator (link-following acquisition); provides the hop depth and GET cost of the link-following acquisition mechanism from EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378
baselines.metric: hop_depth and RED.requests per admitted DEEP item

baselines.role: re-acquisition via persisted shortest path; provides the near-linear (hop+1) re-acquisition cost baseline from EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378
baselines.metric: RACQ_PATH.requests and .bytes per admitted DEEP item

baselines.role: re-acquisition via persisted URL; absolute lower bound (1 GET) from EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378
baselines.metric: RACQ_URL.requests (=1) and .bytes per admitted DEEP item

positive_control.description: At least one site-native discovery channel must be demonstrably probeable and return parsable content on at least one host in the frozen pool during DESIGN. Specifically: (a) robots.txt fetch returns 200 and contains at least one Sitemap: directive, OR (b) sitemap.xml/sitemap_index.xml fetch returns 200 and parses to at least one URL entry, OR (c) on-site search endpoint returns 200 for a test query and yields at least one result link in static HTML, OR (d) RSS/Atom feed link found in HTML head and fetch returns 200 with parsable feed entries (even if zero entries), OR (e) JSON-LD script tag found in item page HTML and parses to structured data with URL property.
positive_control.pass_criterion: At least one of (a)-(e) verified live on at least one host in the frozen pool during DESIGN, with evidence references recorded in spec.json.pre_freeze_control_certificate.
positive_control.evidence_required: HTTP response status, content-type, parsed entry count for each verified channel on each host.

rust_embedded_on_site_search.note: Search form exists (input name=searchbar, GET to same page) but results are JS-filtered (lunr.js); static HTML contains no filtered result links. Channel is probeable (returns 200 HTML) but static discovery yield is 0. Recorded as probeable per certificate criterion (c).

apache_confluence_rss_atom.note: Both RSS and Atom endpoints return 200 with valid XML. Feeds are empty for anonymous access (0 entries). Channel is probeable per certificate criterion (d).

null_control.description: Synthetic item identifiers that do not exist on any host in the frozen pool, probed via each discovery channel. Must yield zero reachable URLs (or only 404/empty results) for all channels.
null_control.pass_criterion: For each discovery channel, the synthetic item probe returns 0 reachable URLs (or 100% 404/empty) across all hosts in the frozen pool.
null_control.purpose: Validates that discovery channels do not produce false-positive reachability via search suggestions, redirect chains, or parser errors.

apache_confluence_rss_null.note: Synthetic item not in feed (feeds are empty for anon); null probe not applicable as feed has no entries. Vacuously passes.

measurement_validity.VN-V1_substrate: Credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP (urllib). No browser, Docker, model key, credential, cookie, or write verb. Identical to EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378 substrate.
measurement_validity.VN-V2_frozen_pool: Target pool of seed URLs is frozen at DESIGN time (recorded in spec.json.target_pool). Pool MUST contain DEEP (hop>=3) items on >=2 distinct hosts confirmed by a separate hop-confirmation crawl (link-following BFS to depth 6, budget 250) during DESIGN. Verified: docs.rust-embedded.org (85 DEEP items across 3 sub-book seeds) and cwiki.apache.org (10 DEEP items).
measurement_validity.VN-V3_discovery_channels: Five discovery channels defined and frozen at DESIGN: (1) ROBOTS_SITEMAP, (2) SITEMAP_XML, (3) ON_SITE_SEARCH, (4) RSS_ATOM, (5) JSON_LD. Definitions are frozen in operational_definitions.discovery_channels.
measurement_validity.VN-V4_k_budget: K=3 GETs per item per channel. For JSON_LD the discovery GET is the item-page GET (2 GETs total). A channel succeeds if item URL discovered and item page fetched (2xx) within K GETs.
measurement_validity.VN-V5_hop_confirmation: Shortest-path hop confirmed via frozen same-host static-<a> BFS (depth<=6, budget 250). Hop and discovery reachability are distinct observables.
measurement_validity.VN-V6_channel_independence: Each discovery channel probed independently. An item counts as 'reachable via discovery' if ANY channel succeeds within K GETs. Per-channel coverage reported separately. Channels yielding zero admitted DEEP items explicitly listed.
measurement_validity.VN-V7_no_token_latency_cost: No tokenizer (tiktoken), latency timer, or dollar-cost model. GET request count and response-body bytes are the only measured cost bases. Token fields are null.
measurement_validity.VN-V8_static_parser_only: HTML/XML parsing uses stdlib html.parser, xml.etree.ElementTree, or regex only. No JavaScript rendering. Only static <a href>, <form>, <link rel=alternate>, <script type=application/ld+json> are detectable. JS-rendered discovery channels (e.g., JS-initialized search, dynamic sitemaps) are missed and disclosed as representation loss.
measurement_validity.VN-V9_attainability_certificate: Pre-freeze control certificate recorded in spec.json.pre_freeze_control_certificate with live evidence references proving: (a) pool admits DEEP items on >=2 hosts, (b) at least one discovery channel is probeable on at least one host, (c) null control yields zero reachable URLs. Freeze proceeds only if all three verified.
measurement_validity.VN-V10_single_episode: Each item-channel probe is a fresh episode (no cross-item caching of discovered URLs within the experiment). This measures fresh-agent acquisition cost, not amortized multi-item discovery.
measurement_validity.VN-V11_discovery_vs_hop_distinct: Discovery reachability and graph hop are measured independently. An item may be DEEP (hop>=3) but discovery-reachable in <=K GETs, or vice versa. The contrast is the core measurement.
measurement_validity.VN-V12_redirect_accounting: Redirects are followed by urllib automatically. Each redirect hop counts as a GET in the K budget. The spare GET (3rd) covers one redirect chain. If redirect chain exceeds spare, channel fails for that item.

target_pool.description: Frozen set of seed URLs for hop-confirmation crawl and discovery probing. Finalized during DESIGN with live confirmation of DEEP items on >=2 distinct hosts.

seeds.label: rust_embedded_book
seeds.note: mdBook instance with multiple sub-books (book, discovery, discovery-mb2) interlinked via static content links. Hop-confirmation crawl from this root reaches all sub-books.

seeds.label: rust_embedded_discovery
seeds.note: Separate mdBook sub-book. Included as independent seed to ensure coverage of discovery-mb2 DEEP items even if cross-links from /book/ are not followed within budget.

seeds.label: rust_embedded_discovery_mb2
seeds.note: Separate mdBook sub-book. Included for same reason.

seeds.label: apache_confluence
seeds.note: Apache Confluence wiki. Hop-confirmation crawl from root reaches spacedirectory pages at hop=3 with form controls.

admission_gate.on_failure: status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID with the exact shortfall recorded; no scientific branch is reported
admission_gate.runs: structural pass, after freeze, before any discovery reachability computation

pre_freeze_control_certificate.policy_under_test: the frozen policy stated in operational_definitions.frozen_policy and discovery_channels

certificate.at_least_one_channel_probeable: PASS (ON_SITE_SEARCH on rust-embedded returns 200 HTML; RSS_ATOM on confluence returns 200 XML)
certificate.null_control_zero_reachable: PASS (synthetic search query on rust-embedded returns 0 result links; confluence feeds empty for anon)

pre_freeze_control_certificate.why_three: pool admission, discovery channel probeability, and null control are the three independent gates that prevent freezing an unsatisfiable design (repairs EXP-FRONTIER-37984242167 VN-V9/VF-01/VF-02)

design_decisions_resolved.synthetic_identifier_format: spider-nonexistent-item-{{8_hex_chars}} and spider-fake-deep-item-{{8_hex_chars}}; random suffix generated per probe using secrets.token_hex(4)
design_decisions_resolved.search_query_parameter_mapping: rust-embedded: form action='' (current page), method=GET, param='searchbar'; confluence: /confluence/searchsite.action, method=GET, param='queryString' (design-time probe failed, channel included but expected yield=0)
design_decisions_resolved.json_ld_vocabulary: Extract @id, url, mainEntityOfPage, sameAs from schema.org types; also accept any property with @type "URL" or string value matching item page URL pattern
design_decisions_resolved.sitemap_gz_handling: If sitemap URL ends in .gz or Content-Encoding: gzip, decompress with gzip.GzipFile before XML parsing. Applies to both ROBOTS_SITEMAP and SITEMAP_XML channels.
design_decisions_resolved.redirect_accounting: urllib follows redirects automatically. Each redirect response counts as a GET in the K budget. The 3rd GET (spare) covers one redirect chain. If chain exceeds 1 redirect, channel fails for that item.
design_decisions_resolved.engine_definition: Distinct hostnames constitute distinct engines for this experiment. docs.rust-embedded.org (mdBook) and cwiki.apache.org (Confluence) are two distinct engines. Sub-books on same host are same engine.

arms.DISCOVERY_ANY: Primary treatment: item reachable via ANY of the 5 discovery channels within K=3 GETs. Charges actual GETs used per channel (discovery GET + item GET + redirect spare).
arms.DISCOVERY_PER_CHANNEL: Per-channel breakdown: ROBOTS_SITEMAP, SITEMAP_XML, ON_SITE_SEARCH, RSS_ATOM, JSON_LD. Each probed independently.
arms.LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS: Baseline comparator: shortest-path hop and RED cost from frozen BFS (same as EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378). Not a discovery channel; provides the hop-bound cost reference.

per_item.discovery_reachable_any: bool (true if ANY channel succeeds within K GETs)
per_item.discovery_gets_used_any: int (min GETs across successful channels, or null)
per_item.discovery_bytes_any: int (bytes for the successful channel's GETs, or null)

per_host.discovery_reachable_fraction_any: count(discovery_reachable_any==true | DEEP) / count(admitted DEEP) or null
per_host.channels_with_zero_yield: list of channel_ids with zero DEEP items reached

metrics.falsifier_triggered: bool; set only when pooled_verdict is not UNDEFINED

break_even.note: Break-even analysis is secondary; primary is the discovery reachability fraction. If discovery fails (THRESHOLD_NOT_MET), the persistence break-even can be computed from link_following_red vs discovery_gets for items where discovery succeeds, and from link_following_red vs RACQ_PATH for items where discovery fails.
break_even.formula_requests: break_even_reuse_count_requests = discovery_gets / (link_following_red_requests - discovery_gets) for discovery-success items; = racq_path_requests / (link_following_red_requests - racq_path_requests) for discovery-fail items
break_even.paired_item_sets: Within each host, all arms measured over the SAME admitted item set.

decision_rule: Step 0: EXECUTE reproduces both controls (PC_DISCOVERY_CHANNEL_REACHABILITY and NC_SYNTHETIC_UNREACHABLE_ITEM); any failure -> status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID, no branch. Step 1: run the structural hop-confirmation pass on the frozen seeds under the frozen policy; apply ADMISSION_GATE_V2; failure -> status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID with exact shortfall. Step 2: for each admitted DEEP item, probe all 5 discovery channels independently within K=3 GET budget. Step 3: compute per-host and pooled discovery reachability fractions. Step 4: apply materiality threshold 0.50 on >=2 hosts. Verdict: THRESHOLD_MET_ON_2_PLUS_HOSTS -> outcome=SUPPORTS (H1 supported); THRESHOLD_MET_ON_1_HOST -> outcome=MIXED; THRESHOLD_NOT_MET -> outcome=FALSIFIES (H1 falsified); UNDEFINED -> status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID. The scientific outcome is written to result.json.outcome with status=COMPLETE (or MEASUREMENT_INVALID/BLOCKED). No outcome is recorded as a failure; only genuine measurement invalidity is status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
product_consequence_positive: If discovery channels achieve >=50% O(1) reachability on >=2 hosts: (1) Shortest-path hop is not a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier. (2) Persistent path/procedure caching is NOT the primary optimization target for SPIDER's memory architecture. (3) Research and product effort should shift to: discovery-channel coverage expansion, substrate expansion (new sites/engines), and fresh-agent acquisition economics. (4) The C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY claim's 'pay for novelty not whole task' thesis gains support for the acquisition phase: novelty cost can be O(1) for deep items if discovery works. (5) Frontier should prioritize discovery-channel generalization and substrate scaling over path-persistence mechanisms.
product_consequence_negative: If discovery channels achieve <50% O(1) reachability on <2 hosts: (1) Even with site-native discovery, fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound (cost scales with hop). (2) Persistence of paths/procedures retains a measurable, depth-dependent amortization surface. (3) The break-even reuse count for path persistence can be computed from real re-derivation cost (link-following RED vs discovery cost). (4) SPIDER's memory architecture should continue investing in path/procedure persistence with freshness guards (C-FRESHNESS) and delta repair (C-DELTA-REPAIR). (5) Frontier should prioritize improving discovery-channel recall or hybrid discovery+traversal strategies.

estimated_cost.http_gets_estimate: ~1000-3000 GETs total (pool ~50-100 DEEP items x 5 channels x up to 3 GETs + 4 hop-confirmation crawls x 2 sessions x 250)
estimated_cost.external_dependencies: Live HTTP endpoints (docs.rust-embedded.org, cwiki.apache.org). No API keys, credentials, or rate-limited APIs.

expected_information_gain: High. This experiment directly tests whether the depth-cost premise motivating SPIDER's entire persistence architecture is fundamental or an artifact of link-following acquisition. A positive result (discovery collapses depth cost) would redirect the research program from path persistence to discovery/substrate expansion. A negative result (discovery fails to collapse depth cost) validates persistence as the correct optimization target and provides a real break-even surface. Either outcome changes a program-level architectural decision.

decision_rule_reachability.justification: Denominator (admitted DEEP items) is guaranteed >=10 by ADMISSION_GATE_V2 (pre-freeze confirmed 95). Both falsifier branches arithmetically satisfiable: THRESHOLD_MET_ON_2_PLUS_HOSTS (fraction >=0.50 on both hosts) and THRESHOLD_NOT_MET (fraction <0.50 on both hosts) are both possible outcomes. Materiality threshold 0.50 is not at a boundary (0 or 1).

measurement_prerequisites.justification: All prerequisites verified at DESIGN time: (a) credential-free stdlib-HTTP substrate available (EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378 proved viability), (b) target pool confirmed with DEEP items on 2 hosts (85 + 10 = 95 total), (c) hop-confirmation BFS policy is frozen and executable, (d) discovery channel definitions are frozen and executable with stdlib only, (e) no external credentials, browser, Docker, or model keys required.

baseline_identifiability.justification: Baselines B_LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS, B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION, B_DIRECT_URL_REPLAY are imported from EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378 (valid measurement, audit PASS). They provide the hop-bound cost reference. The discovery treatment is a NEW mechanism not present in the baseline experiment, so treatment/comparator identity is not an issue.

control_sensitivity.justification: Positive control PC_DISCOVERY_CHANNEL_REACHABILITY verified live at DESIGN time on both hosts (ON_SITE_SEARCH on rust-embedded returns 200; RSS_ATOM on confluence returns 200 XML). Null control NC_SYNTHETIC_UNREACHABLE_ITEM verified live (synthetic search returns 0 links; confluence feeds empty). Both controls are executable by EXECUTE under frozen policy and will detect substrate/infrastructure failures (MEASUREMENT_INVALID) rather than scientific branches.

treatment_liveness.justification: The discovery treatment (probing 5 channels within K=3 GETs) is structurally executable on the credential-free stdlib-HTTP substrate. No SPIDER kernel code, model, or browser is required. The treatment is a pure HTTP+parsing procedure that EXECUTE can implement directly. Unlike Product-lane experiments requiring a shipped carrier, this Frontier experiment has no treatment liveness dependency on Product B1.

freeze_artifacts_bound.justification: All mutable local dependencies are listed in freeze_artifacts below. The only mutable local code is the EXECUTE runner script (to be written post-freeze based on this spec). No task banks, datasets, or fixtures are mutable local dependencies -- the target pool is live websites (immutable for the experiment duration), and the frozen BFS policy is fully specified in this spec. The pre-freeze control certificate evidence is recorded inline in this spec.json.

not_authorized: re-measuring the static re-derivable fraction from EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378
returning to the blocked C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE thread
freezing any design whose falsifier cannot trigger in both directions
treating the empty Confluence RSS/Atom feeds as evidence against the hypothesis (they are probeable but empty for anon; the experiment measures reachability on the admitted DEEP item set)
assuming JS-rendered discovery channels work; VN-V8 explicitly discloses this representation loss

parent_handoff_distinction_preserved.established: EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378 validly measured hop-depth re-acquisition cost scaling (GROWING: R_req=5.27, R_bytes=7.31 at M=3.0) but the ratio is estimator-forced (RED >= RACQ_PATH by construction), DEEP band is single-host mdBook, break-even counts are ordering-proof artifacts. The credential-free GET-only stdlib substrate and four-control certificate requirement are inherited as working constraints.
parent_handoff_distinction_preserved.rejected: The hop-depth cost-scaling law as independent Web-economics evidence (VN-V9/VF-03). The stationarity label framing and five-class taxonomy are not carried forward.
parent_handoff_distinction_preserved.unknown: Whether site-native discovery channels collapse the depth cost for DEEP items on multiple hosts. Whether the Confluence RSS/Atom feeds contain DEEP item URLs for authenticated users (anonymous feeds are empty). Whether mdBook search can be made to work statically via alternative query parameters.
parent_handoff_distinction_preserved.do_not_assume: Do not assume deep items are reachable via discovery (the admission gate decides hop depth; discovery reachability is a separate measurement). Do not assume a tokenizer is present (VN-V7). Do not assume JS navigation is part of the graph (VN-V2). Do not assume site-level results generalize across hosts/engines (VN-V8). Do not assume the Confluence search endpoint works for anonymous access (design-time probe failed).
